title: Back-of-the-Envelope Capacity Estimation
intro: Accurate back-of-the-envelope estimation grounds system design interviews in mathematical reality, sizing compute, storage, memory, and bandwidth.
objectives: Derive Peak QPS from Daily Active Users (DAU) and read-to-write ratios.
Calculate disk storage growth over 5-year retention horizons with replication multipliers.
Apply the 80/20 Pareto principle to size Redis RAM working sets.
body:
### The Estimation Playbook

#### 1. QPS Sizing

#### 2. Storage Growth

23	ext{5-Year Storage} = 	ext{Daily Storage} 	imes 365 	imes 5 	imes 	ext{Replication Factor (3)}23

#### 3. RAM Cache Sizing (80/20 Rule)
20% of the daily read requests generate 80% of the traffic. Cache the top 20% in memory:
23	ext{Cache RAM} = 	ext{Daily Read Volume} 	imes 0.20 	imes 1.25 	ext{ (25% buffer)}23
keyIdea: Use powers of two approximations (^{10}=1KB, 2^{20}=1MB, 2^{30}=1GB$). Never guess; derive all numbers systematically.

concepts.title: Key Latency Numbers
concepts.body: L1 cache: 0.5ns, Main Memory (RAM): 100ns, SSD random read: 150us, Cross-datacenter RTT: 150ms.

concepts.title: Seconds in a Day
concepts.body: 86,400 seconds ~ 100,000 seconds for quick mental approximations.

examples: Twitter: 300M DAU * 5 tweets/day = 1.5B writes/day = ~17,500 write QPS.

quiz.prompt: If a system has 100M daily writes and each write is 1KB, approximately how much raw storage is required per day?
